name: Graham Kessler
career: Sign painter and mural lettering specialist
bio: Graham spends most weekdays hand-lettering restaurant walls, storefront windows, and event backdrops, then unwinds at night by lifting, drilling Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, or sketching logo ideas in a beat-up notebook. He has a soft spot for old-school rap, R&B slow jams, and 80s-90s nostalgia, and he's the kind of person who will pause everything for a great Hot Ones interview or a funny clip someone sends the group chat. Faith is a steady part of his week, and he talks openly about wanting a deeply affectionate, ride-or-die relationship and eventually becoming the kind of father who shows up for everything. A mildly unexpected detail: he keeps a growing collection of vintage enamel paint signs in his garage and restores them by hand on weekends.

user_voice.natural_register: Warm, grounded, and conversational with a blue-collar creative streak. He writes like someone talking from the shop, the gym, or the couch after a long day: direct, encouraging, lightly funny, and sincere without trying to sound polished. He tends to sound appreciative and observant, especially when talking about craft, training, faith, music, or relationships.
user_voice.punctuation_habits: Mostly standard sentence punctuation with occasional dashes or ellipses when thinking out loud. Uses exclamation points sparingly for genuine hype, not every line. He'll keep things readable rather than stylized, and may use short sentence fragments for emphasis.
user_voice.humor_tone: Easygoing and playful, more amused than snarky. He likes meme-level humor, light roasting, and 'man that's wild' reactions, but not mean-spirited dunks.
user_voice.voice_avoid: He avoids overly online slang, detached irony, and fake-inspirational corporate speak. He also doesn't come off confessional-for-attention; even when he's being heartfelt, he keeps it grounded and doesn't trauma-dump or posture.

use_purposes: keep up with design and fight content
Instagram.audience_lens: A mix of real-life friends, fellow artists, training people, and casual followers who mostly know him through visuals.
Instagram.style_description: Here the shared voice gets a little tighter and more visual because the post usually starts with an image or reel. He gives enough context to feel personal, but not a full story; appreciation for craft, progress, or a good moment tends to lead.

expression.audience_self_censoring: He keeps heavier relationship longing, deeper faith reflection, and family-dream talk mostly in the background unless the post clearly calls for it.
expression.emoji_topic_filter: Most often pulls from 🎨, 💪, 🔥, 🙌, 😂 depending on whether he's posting work, training, or reacting to a reel.

Instagram.app_avoid: He usually skips long explanatory shop talk or vulnerable life essays here because the audience is scrolling for quick visual context.

use_purposes: check in with family and old friends
react to sports and nostalgia content
Facebook.audience_lens: This is the broadest and most personal audience: relatives, old classmates, family friends, and people who know his life more than his aesthetic.
Facebook.style_description: The same voice gets a little fuller and more contextual here because he's writing to people who actually know him, not just his interests. This is where gratitude, family-mindedness, faith, and milestone-style updates surface more naturally than performance or niche hobby talk.

expression.audience_self_censoring: He tones down fight-fan trash talk, thirstier relationship commentary, and anything that could read too online or too inside-baseball for older relatives.

Facebook.app_avoid: He avoids sounding too sarcastic or hyper-online here because family and longtime acquaintances are the ones most likely reading.

use_purposes: live react to sports or fights
join casual humor or culture conversation
Threads.audience_lens: Mostly strangers and loose mutuals who share his interests, with much less personal history attached.
Threads.style_description: On Threads his voice gets shorter, quicker, and more reactive because the platform rewards instant takes over full context. The same sincerity is still there, but it comes out as sharper observations, quick jokes, or real-time hype around fights, football, music, or random funny stuff.

expression.audience_self_censoring: He usually leaves out deeper personal values, faith nuance, and earnest relationship goals because that audience is there for reactions, not autobiography.
expression.emoji_topic_filter: Sports and fight reactions make 🥊, 🏈, 🔥, 😂 surface more than the rest of his palette.

Threads.app_avoid: He avoids detailed mural-process posts or long personal reflection threads here because the public audience is mainly there for quick takes.

Chatbot.style_description: In private, the same voice becomes more utilitarian and transparent about what he actually needs help with. He gives more context, asks follow-up questions, and is more willing to admit uncertainty around work decisions, relationships, self-improvement, or faith-related reflection.

expression.audience_self_censoring: He doesn't need to hide much here, but he still tends to ask in a practical, solution-oriented way instead of spiraling dramatically.

Chatbot.app_avoid: He avoids performative wording here; if he's using a chatbot, he wants clarity and usefulness more than vibe.

events.specific_situation: Graham has been thinking harder about how much of his gender history and bisexuality to share on dating apps and with new people. He’s trying to balance being open with protecting himself, especially after a few awkward conversations that made him second-guess what he wants to say up front.

hidden_persona_summary: Beneath his public engagement, he reads as someone quietly organizing his identity around two stabilizing hopes: being unmistakably chosen in a deeply loyal, affectionate partnership and building a grounded, well-made life around home, family, and fatherhood. That hidden layer shows up in the very private way he lingers on idealized relationship and domestic content—especially #RelationshipGoals, #couplegoals, #loveofmylife, #familygoals, #tinyhomes, and #smallspaces—while more openly consuming humor, sports, and culture content that let him project confidence, taste, and connection without overexposing vulnerability. His visible interests in 90s/2000s rap legacy media, R&B, design inspiration, and interview platforms like Hot Ones are not random; the private pull toward #Camron, #JayZ, #HipHopLegends, #DrinkChamps, and #TheBreakfastClub suggests he uses old-school Black media nostalgia as a masculine self-styling anchor, while the heavy volume of #funnyvideos, #comedy, #relatable, and #FunnyMoments points to humor as an everyday bonding tool and emotional regulator. Publicly, he is more legible through football, UFC/MMA, BJJ, WWE, grilling, faith, fatherhood, and shareable comedy, whereas privately he appears to save his most emotionally charged attention for couple devotion, family security, and compact sanctuary imagery; there is no validated evidence here of medical or aesthetic-medicine engagement such as tretinoin use, GLP-1 treatment, or other named routines.

E_I.reason: He engages publicly with broadly shareable content, but the most emotionally loaded themes are kept private and inward-facing, suggesting a stronger introverted than extraverted orientation.

S_N.reason: His interests include concrete entertainment, sports, and home aesthetics, but the hidden pattern of idealized future-building, identity symbolism, and private longing points slightly more toward abstract, possibility-focused intuition.

T_F.reason: The strongest signals are relational and value-driven—loyal partnership, fatherhood, belonging, and emotional security—while humor and masculine styling appear to support connection rather than detached analysis.

J_P.reason: He shows some organizing preferences around home, family, and a grounded life, but the overall pattern feels more exploratory and content-driven than tightly structured, giving a slight edge to Perceiving.
